newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-TONGA FACE TOUGH TASK AGAINST SOUTH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TONGA FACE TOUGH TASK AGAINST SOUTH AFRICA.

text.p: Pacific island side Tonga, missing eight of their first-choice players, are expected to provide soft opposition for South Africa at Newlands on Tuesday in the Springboks' first match under new coach Carel du Plessis.

Although Tonga arrived in South Africa fresh from victories over the Zimbabwe Goshawks, Zimbabwe, a Namibian Development side and Namibia over the previous fortnight, they have failed to convince in their three tour matches building up to the one-off test.
The opening fixture of their brief tour saw the Tongans overpowered 46-6 by lowly North West in icy conditions in Potchefstroom.
They then bounced back to beat an Eastern Province invitation side 34-19 eight days ago, followed by a 27-10 victory over Border last Wednesday night.
Although the islanders did impress with their robust game and punishing tackling in the midfield, all three games were against minor South African provincial sides.
Significantly Tonga, who will be watched in Cape Town on Tuesday by All Black wing Jonah Lomu, are missing several key players who are committed to rugby contracts in Japan and the United States.
Probably their best-known absentee is 1995 World Cup lock Ipolito Fenukitau, who was unable to tour Southern Africa because of Super 12 commitments with Australian Capital Territory.
While the 1997-style Springboks will not be taking their Tongan opponents lightly, their forthcoming test matches against the British Lions are uppermost in their minds.

"A test match is always a test match and we certainly can't underestimate Tonga. But we're obviously building towards the test series against the Lions - and that's our priority at the moment," South African captain Gary Teichmann told Reuters.

The performance of the Springboks against the Tongans will come under a great deal of scrutiny after the pledge by new coach du Plessis to adopt a more flexible style of running rugby than his predecessors.
Du Plessis shocked the South African rugby fraternity by omitting World Cup Springboks Hennie le Roux and Kobus Wiese from Tuesday's line-up.

Griqualand West centre Edrich Lubbe makes his international debut against Tonga alongside the solid Japie Mulder while Western Province lock Fritz van Heerden and Free State hooker Naka Drotske both earn recalls.

South Africa: Andre Joubert; James Small, Japie Mulder, Edrich Lubbe, Andre Snyman; Henry Honiball, Joost van der Westhuizen; Gary Teichmann (captain), Andre Venter, Ruben Kruger, Fritz van Heerden, Hannes Strydom, Adrian Garvey, Naka Drotske, Os du Rndt.
Substitutes: Russell Bennett, Boeta Wessels, Werner Swanepoel, Mark Andrews, James Dalton, Dawie Theron.

Tonga (probable): Gustavo Tonga; Semisi Faka'osifolau, Viliami Uhi, Chris Schumkel, Sione Moalatu; Siua Taumalolo, Manu Vunipola; Kilioni Tu'ipulotu, Sione Tohi, Maama Molitika, Kuli Faletau, 'Alipate Ta'ufo'ou, Heamani Lavaka, Fe'ao Vunipola, Ngaslu au.
